abstract: Cortical activity exhibits diverse timescales that vary with behavioral state, but the underlying circuit mechanisms remain unclear. Analyzing Allen Institute Neuropixels recordings from mouse primary visual cortex, we found that the fraction of excitatory neurons activated by optogenetic stimulation of somatostatin (SST) interneurons varied across mice. Intrinsic timescales lengthened during arousal in mice with a lower fraction of activated excitatory neurons and shortened in those with a higher fraction. To investigate a possible mechanism, we trained spiking networks with cell-type-specific plasticity, producing configurations dominated by direct SST inhibition of excitatory neurons or indirect disinhibition via parvalbumin interneurons. Arousal-like input to vasoactive intestinal peptide (VIP) interneurons slowed assembly dynamics, lengthened intrinsic timescales, and accelerated assembly formation when direct inhibition dominated, with opposite effects when indirect disinhibition dominated. Our results suggest that the balance between these pathways can account for opposite timescale responses to arousal and shape its computational consequences.
